title: Adequately affine morphism of algebraic stacks
statement: Work in the universe and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$ be algebraic stacks over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ be a morphism. Use quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness from [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], and quasi-coherent algebras, surjections and global sections from [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. The smooth-etale site $\operatorname{Lis-et}(\mathcal V)$ has objects smooth morphisms $T\to\mathcal V$ from schemes; an arrow from $T\to\mathcal V$ to $T'\to\mathcal V$ is a scheme map $T\to T'$ together with a $2$-isomorphism of its composite to the given map, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Its covering families are families whose underlying scheme maps are jointly surjective and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]; site terminology is [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A$ on $\mathcal U$, its direct image on the smooth-etale site of $\mathcal V$ has value $\Gamma(\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}T,\mathcal A|_{\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}T})$ on a smooth scheme test $T\to\mathcal V$, with restrictions by pullback. Smooth means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] on scheme charts. A map $\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ of sheaves of algebras on this site is universally adequate if, for every such test $T$ and $t\in\mathcal D(T)$, there exist an etale covering family $T_i\to T$, integers $N_i>0$ and $s_i\in\mathcal C(T_i)$ mapping to $(t|_{T_i})^{N_i}$; etale coverings use [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The morphism $f$ is adequately affine if it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and, for every surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal U$, the induced $f_*\mathcal A\to f_*\mathcal B$ is universally adequate. The quantifier includes arbitrary quasi-coherent algebras, without finite-generation restrictions.

from.place: det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Affine PGL quotients with closed orbits and zero-dimensional stabilizers. Supporting affine-quotient step: Finite diagonal from an affine adequate moduli space. Supporting input: the adequate moduli space for the product, before the finiteness criterion; Q44 product-affinization proof: the notion used in Proposition 4.2.1, before taking the product
